texts: good. the conditional becomes a rule that can actually fire: any lantern burning mire-essence gets its own producing event, and 'the lantern' in the second half correctly refers back to the one that is burning.
good. the 'whenever' wording lands on the same fireable rule as the 'when' version, with a giving event minted for each burning occasion and mist-light as what is given.

mixed: the content is all there (mist-light is a flame, and it is pale and it is silver), but the two colour words were recorded as exceptionless definitions rather than ordinary general properties, which is a calibration fault on our side that no rewrite would change. What your wording does leave open is whether 'pale silver' is one shade or two separate properties; the parse guessed two, so if that is what you mean, write 'Mist-light is a flame, and it is pale and silver.' to make it explicit.
good. it becomes a rule that denies the producing for every ordinary oil, and the 'ordinary' restriction is kept as part of the condition rather than quietly dropped.
